market_context: US/Canada audience; fatigue from repeated pregnancy check-ins.
title: Getting tired of everyone constantly asking how your pregnancy is going

seo.title: Tired of everyone asking how your pregnancy is going?
seo.meta_description: Repeated check-ins can be exhausting even when they are loving. Reduce the load with short responses, fewer updates, and permission to change the subject.
seo.search_intent: Support pregnant women who are exhausted by constant questions about pregnancy.

excerpt: A caring question can still become exhausting when you answer it ten times a week. You do not owe every person a fresh emotional and physical update.
content_html:
“How are things going?” can be a genuinely kind question. The fatigue appears when it opens every text thread, family gathering, and phone call, leaving you to give the same update again and again. What is a small gesture for each person can become repetitive emotional labor for you.

You can appreciate the intention without being available for the full conversation every time.

Notice the cumulative workload, not just each individual question

No single check-in may be intrusive. The exhaustion comes from the sum: reviewing how you feel, turning it into an answer, reassuring other people, and opening a conversation you did not always want.

Create a default response

“Everything is moving along, thanks for asking” or “no major updates” can be a complete answer. You do not need to report symptoms, appointments, or emotions because someone asked.

Centralize updates only if that actually helps you

Some families use a small group chat for occasional updates, which can reduce individual messages. But you do not have to create a newsletter if your real preference is to discuss pregnancy less.

Protect conversations that give something back to you

You can answer briefly and then ask, “How are you?” or move to a shared interest. If a friendship has become almost entirely pregnancy talk, saying you miss other topics may improve the relationship.

Care and attention do not have to disappear; they can become broader. Being pregnant does not require your physical status to be the opening subject of every interaction.

faq.question: Am I ungrateful if constant questions annoy me?
faq.answer: No. You can appreciate people's care and still feel exhausted by repetition.

faq.question: Do I have to explain how I feel every time?
faq.answer: No. A brief general response is enough when you do not want to discuss details.

faq.question: What can I do with relatives who ask every day?
faq.answer: You can request less frequent check-ins or say you will send updates when there is something you want to share.
